projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

This pattern indicates a social gathering rather than the family being alone.

The sustained high device presence (21-23) paired with zero camera motion over several hours strongly suggests the cameras are offline, obstructed, or the family is entirely in a single non-camera zone, warranting a quick verification of camera feeds or family location.

The sustained high device count (22–25) paired with zero camera motion or activity over the observed period points to either a network reporting glitch, many IoT devices connected, or residents confined to camera-blind zones. This recurring pattern aligns with earlier flagged jumps and warrants monitoring for connectivity instability or unreported guests.

Connected devices jumped from ~22 to 26-27 between 16:39 and 17:11 with zero camera motion throughout the entire window, suggesting new devices connected without triggering visual sensors. Verify if visitors arrived via a camera-blind entry or if smart home devices recently rebooted.

Connected devices rose from 17 to 22-23 between 1:44 PM and 3:00 PM with zero camera motion, indicating either new smart devices or tablets joining the network, or visitors arriving in camera-blind spots. Verify camera status or check for unexpected guests.

The steady decline in connected devices from ~22 to 17, followed by a stable count and zero camera motion, indicates the household has likely consolidated into a single room or zone for a shared activity rather than leaving the house.

The gradual decline in connected devices (22 to 17) paired with zero camera activity indicates a planned, gradual departure from the home, consistent with a normal Wednesday school and work schedule rather than an unexpected event.

The sustained drop in connected devices from ~23 to 20 between 08:33 and 08:59, paired with zero camera motion, indicates the household is likely departing for school or work without triggering motion alerts, consistent with a typical Wednesday morning routine.

The device count jump to 24 at 05:21 AM, combined with zero camera activity and Steve’s 2.39h sleep record, confirms he has been awake in bed using personal devices for nearly 40 minutes while the rest of the household remains asleep. This coherent pattern indicates a quiet pre-dawn state rather than an early departure, but his prolonged wakefulness suggests he may need a gentle morning routine prompt later.

Zero camera activity and stable device presence confirm the household environment is completely undisturbed, isolating Steve’s acute sleep loss and low HRV (98) as internal stress or insomnia rather than an external disruption. He will likely experience significant morning fatigue and reduced cognitive function.
